svg.text: Adverse selection: a higher price buys a costlier clientele

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The price decides who buys; the buyers' mean cost rises by 1/(2β) for each unit of price

svg.text: A unit price rise moves the threshold by 1/β = 0.5

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and lifts mean buyer cost by 1/(2β) = 0.25.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Profit per sale rises by only 1 − 1/(2β) = 0.75.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The heavy segment is who buys: only c ≥ 0.45, i.e. 55% of the market. Anyone below the price line values the good less than the price.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Microsoft YaHei', 'PingFang SC', 'Noto Sans SC', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: So buyers are not a random sample but the costliest group. Drawn with α = 0.1, β = 2.
